 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.796 of 2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.05.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 01.05.2014 at about 10.30 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle through M.C road, a car bearing Registration No.KL-12/D-7548 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on his motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver cum owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.10,20,000/- limited to Rs.7,00,000/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the MACA NO. 2443 OF 2017 2025:KER:32496 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10 and C1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,06,058/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.Elson Simon, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

As per the claim petition, the petitioner was Jishnu vs United India Insurance Co.Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84666166/

sentences.text: 11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.9,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.9,500/-.
12. In the accident the petitioner sustained compound fracture left femur, fracture medial malleolus and tallus.
ACL rupture (L) and laceartion over scalp and left elbow.
Wound debridement and suturing with ORIF, ILN + MCL was done.
13. As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, his permanent physical disability was assessed as 9.15%.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 9.15%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 24 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,62,861/-.

15. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.56,000/- being the income for 8 months @
Rs.7,000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 9 months.

Therefore,
towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.85,500/- (9,500 x 9 months).
16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.35,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was MACA NO. 2443 OF 2017 2025:KER:32496 treated as inpatient for 23 days and in the meantime, he had undergone one surgery also.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75,000/-, Rs.60,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
